learning_objective: 🎯 [Students will master the rules of subject-verb agreement, specifically tackling tricky subjects like collective nouns, indefinite pronouns, and compound subjects.]
warm_up_hook: 💃🕺 Think of the Subject and the Verb as dance partners. If the Subject takes a singular step, the Verb must match it. If they don't match, they step on each other's toes! Let's learn the choreography of Concord! 🎶

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Singular subjects take singular verbs (usually ending in -s). Plural subjects take plural verbs. When subjects are joined by 'and', they take a plural verb. EXCEPT when the two nouns form a single idea (e.g., Bread and butter).
examples_or_templates: Plural: The boy and the girl are studying.
Single Idea: Bread and butter is my favorite breakfast.

lesson_modules.teaching_content: When subjects are joined by 'or', 'either...or', or 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the subject CLOSEST to it.
examples_or_templates: Example A: Neither the coach nor the players were happy. ('players' is plural, so 'were')
Example B: Neither the players nor the coach was happy. ('coach' is singular, so 'was')

lesson_modules.teaching_content: Words like Everyone, Someone, Anybody, Nobody, Each, and Every always take singular verbs. Also, plural-looking nouns representing distance, time, weight, or amounts of money take singular verbs.
examples_or_templates: Indefinite: Everyone in the class has completed the test. (Not 'have')
Measurement: Ten miles is a long way to walk. (Not 'are')

practice_mcq_quiz.question: ❓ Which verb completes the sentence correctly? 'Either my brother or my parents _____ going to pick me up.'
❓ Identify the correct sentence:
options: Fifty dollars are too much to pay for a t-shirt.
Fifty dollars is too much to pay for a t-shirt.
Everyone have a right to speak.
The committee are finalizing the report today.
practice_mcq_quiz.correct_answer: Fifty dollars is too much to pay for a t-shirt.

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Correct the error: 'The list of items are on the desk.'
subjective_practice.hint: Identify the actual subject. Is it 'list' or 'items'?

subjective_practice.question: ✍️ Fill in the blank with is/are: 'Neither the principal nor the teachers _____ attending the seminar, but everyone else _____.'
subjective_practice.hint: Apply the proximity rule for the first blank, and the indefinite pronoun rule for the second blank.

activity_or_assignment.title: ✂️ The Grammar Surgeon
activity_or_assignment.instructions: Find a short news article online. Purposefully change 5 verbs so they completely mismatch their subjects (e.g., 'The team are winning' -> 'The team am winning'). Swap with a partner and fix each other's surgical mistakes!

chapter_summary: ⭐ Subjects and verbs must agree in number. Compound subjects with 'and' take plural verbs unless they represent one concept.
⭐ With 'Either/Or' and 'Neither/Nor', the verb matches the noun closest to it.
⭐ Indefinite pronouns (Everyone, Nobody) and measurements (Time, Money, Distance) always take singular verbs.
